newsitem.title: CHINA: Yaohan slows China store expansion.
newsitem.headline: Yaohan slows China store expansion.

text.p: Yaohan International will slow its China expansion, pushing back by one year its plan to have 1,000 stores throughout the Yangtze River delta by the year 2005, a Yaohan official said on Monday.

Hironobu Yasunaga, director and general manager of Yaohan (Shanghai) Holdings Co., said expansion plans would be delayed due to problems in getting licences in new cities and the need for Yaohan China to rely on internal funds for expansion rather than bank loans.
He said the company would instead focus next year on adding stores in Shanghai and nearby Wuxi.
It plans to add between five and 10 new stores in the two cities on top of the existing 33 stores, using internally generated funds, he said.
Shares in Yaohan Japan have fallen steeply this year and its credit rating in Japan has been cut, due in part to its fast expansion into new Asian markets, including China.
"I think people, after looking at our Japanese operation, are sceptical of our China operation, but I believe that we are doing very well here," Yasunaga said.

He said the company's overall target of setting up 1,000 stores throughout the Yangtze delta by 2005, announced in July, had been pushed back by one year, but added it was possible to make up the lost time in the coming years.

"It's not a setback. We will be continuing to open stores in Shanghai and Wuxi by using internally generated funds," Yasunaga said. "The focus will be on strengthening our operations in Shanghai and Wuxi and introducing our own brand."
He said the company hoped that, by the end of 1997, more than 500 of the 4,000 items stocked in Yaohan supermarkets would carry the Yaohan brand.
Yasunaga said the flagship Yaohan store in the Pudong area of east Shanghai, opened just over a year ago, had done 30 percent better business in the second half of 1996 than the first half.
"The store is doing well. Business is growing in line with our expectations," he said, but declined to give detailed figures.
He said Yaohan had so far invested close to $100 million in its China retail ventures, all of which are conducted on a joint-venture basis with local partners.
The Yaohan group formally shifted its corporate headquarters to Shanghai from Hong Kong in July, to symbolise its commitment to the China market.
